brief_summary:
This study compares two physiotherapy treatments to help adults recover movement after total knee replacement: functional massage and passive knee mobilization. The main question is whether functional massage helps patients bend their knee further by the time they leave the acute hospital ward.

Forty adults undergoing replacement of one knee or both knees during the same operation will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will receive functional massage according to Olaf Evjenth, and the other will receive passive manual knee mobilization. Both groups will also receive the same standard rehabilitation and pain management.

The assigned treatment will be provided once daily, starting on the first day after surgery and continuing until hospital discharge. Each treatment will last 10 minutes per operated knee.

A clinician who does not know which treatment the patient received will assess knee movement. The study will also evaluate pain, functional mobility, patient-reported outcomes, and length of hospital stay.
interventions: Functional Massage According to Olaf Evjenth
primary_outcomes: Knee Flexion
title: Functional Massage Versus Passive Mobilization After Total Knee Replacement

brief_summary:
This study is for women planning surgery to repair pelvic organ prolapse.For patients with pelvic organ prolapse accompanied by occult stress urinary incontinence before the operation, the clinical phenomenon of de novo stress urinary incontinence (SUI) after pelvic floor reconstruction is relatively common. It manifests as involuntary leakage of urine during coughing, sneezing, or walking, seriously affecting daily life, social interaction, and physical and mental health.

The pubourethral ligament plication (ULP) is an anti-leakage operation based on autologous tissue repair, without the implantation of synthetic sling. By folding and tightening the pelvic urethral ligament and stimulating local regeneration of new collagen, it repairs the natural urethral support structure.A large number of literature reports have confirmed that its treatment efficacy for patients with preoperative stress urinary incontinence symptoms can reach 90%. Compared with midurethral suspension surgery, ULP takes less operating time, avoids sling-related complications and costs lessly.

However, it is not clear whether this surgical method can significantly reduce the postoperative leakage risk of this group of patients. This trial aims to answer this question and balance its benefits and risks.

The study would be conducted in 5 hospitals in China. Eligible participants would be randomly assigned to two groups:

* The experimental group: received standard prolapse repair surgery and the pubourethral ligament plication（ULP）
* The control group: only received standard prolapse repair surgery

Investigators would conduct the primary assessment 3 months after the surgery. The main objective is to test whether this additional procedure could reduce the occurrence of new urinary leakage after the surgery. Investigators would also follow participants for 1 year, recording urinary symptoms, quality of life, and surgical-related adverse conditions. The doctors responsible for evaluating the outcomes would be blinded to group assignment.

This study has been reviewed and approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) of Peking University People's Hospital.
primary_outcomes: The incidence of overt stress urinary incontinence at 3 months postoperatively between the two groups.
title: The Preventive Efficacy of ULP for Stress Urinary Incontinence After Pelvic Organ Prolapse Surgery

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, prospective, observational clinical study designed to evaluate the real-world efficacy and safety of jaktinib in patients with newly diagnosed myelofibrosis (MF). The primary outcome measure is the proportion of patients achieving anemia response at week 24. Secondary outcome measures include MF-related symptom response rate (TSS50) at week 24, spleen volume reduction ≥35% (SVR35) at week 24, progression-free survival (PFS), leukemia-free survival (LFS), overall survival (OS), and safety/tolerability. This study will provide real-world evidence supporting the use of jaktinib as a first-line treatment for newly diagnosed MF patients.
primary_outcomes: anemia response
title: A Multicenter, Prospective, Observational Study of Jaktinib in Newly Diagnosed Myelofibrosis

brief_summary:
The HOPE (Hopkins Opportunities for Participant Engagement) Research Registry is a free and secure way for adults to learn about research studies at Johns Hopkins and find out about opportunities to participate. HOPE was created to help connect people who are interested in research with Johns Hopkins research teams conducting studies in many different health areas.

Adults age 18 or older who live in the United States may voluntarily join HOPE. To enroll, participants complete a short form that takes about 5 minutes and provide basic information about themselves and the types of research the participant may be interested in. Participants may receive information about new research studies, including studies related to the topics selected.

If a participant is interested in a study, the participant can choose to share contact information with the research team so the team can contact the participant directly. Joining HOPE does not mean that a person has to participate in any research study. Participation in HOPE is voluntary, there is no cost to join, and participants can update information or leave the registry at any time.
primary_outcomes: Number of individuals enrolled in the HOPE Research Registry
title: Research Participant Registry "Hopkins Opportunities for Participant Engagement"

brief_summary:
MS-FatigueCARE is a prospective, multicenter study aimed at investigating the mechanisms underlying fatigue in people with multiple sclerosis (MS) and mild disability, and at evaluating the efficacy of a personalized home-based telerehabilitation program. Fatigue is one of the most debilitating symptoms of MS and can significantly impact daily activities and quality of life, even in individuals with low levels of neurological disability. Current assessment relies primarily on patient-reported measures, highlighting the need for objective and sensitive fatigue biomarkers.

The study comprises two complementary phases. Phase 1 is a cross-sectional observational study comparing people with relapsing-remitting MS and mild disability (EDSS score 0-3.5) with healthy controls. The objective is to investigate the relationship between perceived fatigue and objective physiological and motor parameters, focusing specifically on oxygen consumption (VO₂), the metabolic cost of walking (CW), postural control, and gait-related parameters. In participants with MS, the potential association between fatigue and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) serological status or reactivation will also be examined.

Phase 2 is a single-blind, randomized controlled crossover study involving MS participants who completed Phase 1. Participants will be randomly assigned to either a six-week multidomain telerehabilitation program-based on non-immersive virtual reality and "serious games"-or a self-managed therapeutic education program. The telerehabilitation intervention integrates motor, cognitive, and cardiorespiratory exercises to be performed at home four times a week for 60 minutes, with remote monitoring by rehabilitation professionals. After a six-week washout period, participants will switch to the alternative intervention. The primary outcome is the energy cost of walking, measured during the 6-Minute Walking Test. Secondary outcomes include subjective fatigue, cognitive and psychological functioning, walking and balance performance, quality of life, usability, and treatment adherence, as well as instrumental measures of VO₂/VCO₂, postural control, and lower-limb kinematics.

Overall, MS-FatigueCARE aims to identify objective markers of fatigue and determine whether a personalized, multi-domain telerehabilitation approach can reduce fatigue and improve functional outcomes and quality of life for people with MS, while fostering accessible and continuous rehabilitative care.
primary_outcomes: Cost of walking - CW
title: Tele-rehabilitation Program in People With Multiple Sclerosis and Mild Disability

brief_summary: This study is to understand how well elranatamab (PF-06863135) may be used for relapsed refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). Sometimes MM might improve at first, but then gets resistant to the treatment and starts growing again (known as relapsed refractory). This study medicine will be compared with standard-of-care (SOC) therapies used in real-world clinical practice. For people receiving elranatamab, we will use data from the phase 3 clinical trial (MagnetisMM-5). We will also use data from a real-world database, representing the SOC in clinical practice. This study does not seek any participants for enrollment. We will compare the experiences of people receiving elranatamab to people receiving SOC therapies. This way, it will help us to know how well elranatamab can be used for RRMM treatment.
primary_outcomes: Real World Progression Free Survival (rwPFS)
Overall Survival (OS)
Time to next treatment (TTNT)
title: A Study to Learn About a Medicine (Called Elranatamab) in People With Relapsed Refractory Multiple Myeloma

brief_summary:
Statement of the problem:

Traumatic dental injuries (TDIs) are among the most common dental emergencies encountered in clinical practice and represent a significant burden in both primary and secondary healthcare settings. These injuries frequently affect children and young adults and may lead to long-term functional, aesthetic, and psychological consequences if not managed appropriately. The global burden of TDIs is considerable, with epidemiological studies indicating that a large proportion of individuals experience dental trauma during their lifetime.

Crown fractures are the most frequently reported type of injury, whereas luxation injuries and alveolar bone fractures present greater diagnostic and management challenges.

TDIs are particularly prevalent among school-aged populations due to increased exposure to physical activities, sports injuries, and accidental falls. In addition, delayed or inappropriate management may result in pulpal necrosis, root resorption, or tooth loss, increasing treatment complexity and cost.

Successful management of TDIs requires immediate and accurate diagnosis, correct classification, and evidence-based treatment planning. However, undergraduate dental students often demonstrate limited clinical confidence and inadequate decision-making skills due to insufficient exposure to trauma cases.

Previous studies have identified gaps in knowledge and clinical competence among dental students and interns and general practitioners in managing TDIs. This highlights the need for improved educational strategies.
interventions: This study is a randomized controlled trial with parallel groups with 1:1 allocation ratio.
primary_outcomes: To compare the effectiveness of the DTG learning platform and traditional teaching methods in improving knowledge for management of traumatic dental injuries among a group of dental interns.

To evaluate and compare knowledge for management traumatic dental injuries between the DTG learning platform and traditional teaching methods using Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs). • To assess and compare clinical reasoning skills in management of traum
title: Effectiveness of an Interactive Digital Learning Platform (Dental Trauma Guide) on Knowledge and Clinical Decision-Making Skills in Management of Traumatic Dental Injuries Among a Group of Dental Interns

brief_summary:
This study will compare pain, nausea, and vomiting after keyhole gallbladder removal in adults with symptomatic gallstones.

The study will examine two commonly used methods for entering the abdomen. In the Veress needle method, a thin needle is used to introduce carbon dioxide gas before the first surgical port is inserted. In the direct trocar method, the first surgical port is inserted before the gas is introduced.

Adults aged 18-60 years undergoing planned keyhole gallbladder surgery at Akbar Niazi Teaching Hospital, Islamabad, Pakistan, will be invited to participate. The operating surgeon will choose the entry method according to routine clinical practice and the patient's clinical needs. The research team will record the method used without assigning treatment.

Pain will be assessed at 2, 6, and 24 hours after surgery using a scale from 0, meaning no pain, to 10, meaning the worst imaginable pain. Nausea and vomiting will be recorded during the first 24 hours. Additional pain relief and medicines used to treat nausea or vomiting will also be documented.

The findings may help clinicians understand whether postoperative symptoms differ between these two entry methods.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative pain score
title: Comparison of Postoperative Pain, Nausea, and Vomiting Between Veress Needle and Direct Trocar Entry in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy

brief_summary: This is a randomized, controlled, double-blind, multicenter phase iii clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of enlonstobart, with or without SYS6010 as adjuvant therapy, in participants with pathologically residual esophageal squamous cell carcinoma following complete surgical resection.

title: A Randomized, Controlled, Double-Blind, Multicenter Phase III Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Enlonstobart, With or Without SYS6010 as Adjuvant Therapy, in Participants With Pathologically Residual Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Following Complete Surgical Resection

brief_summary:
Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor and non-motor impairments that negatively affect functional independence and quality of life. Although multimodal rehabilitation approaches have demonstrated therapeutic benefits, underlying pathophysiological mechanisms may limit the magnitude and persistence of treatment effects. In this context, transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance neuroplasticity and optimize motor responses to physical rehabilitation.

This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial aimed to investigate the effects of tDCS combined with Nordic walking as part of a multimodal rehabilitation program on upper limb function in individuals with Parkinson's disease. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either active or sham tDCS, both combined with the same multimodal rehabilitation program over four consecutive weeks. Upper limb motor performance, manual dexterity, handgrip strength, and quality of life were assessed before and after the intervention, as well as at a 30-day follow-up. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, with a significance level of 5%.
primary_outcomes: Change in Upper Limb Motor Function Assessed by the MDS-UPDRS Part III
title: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation Combined With Nordic Walking on Upper Limb Function in Individuals With Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the clinical value of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted medical imaging in the diagnosis and management of focal liver lesions. Accurate diagnosis of focal liver lesions is important for selecting appropriate treatment strategies. However, distinguishing between different types of liver lesions can be challenging because of overlapping imaging features. AI-based imaging systems may help improve diagnostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making.
primary_outcomes: Overall Diagnostic Accuracy of AI-Assisted Versus Conventional Physician Imaging Assessment
title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Imaging for Diagnosis and Management of Focal Liver Lesions

brief_summary:
This observational, cross-sectional study was designed to investigate the relationship between physical activity and mental health among university students, with particular emphasis on the potential mediating roles of perceived social support and self-esteem.

The study included 484 university students (309 males and 175 females). Data were collected through an online survey using standardized self-report questionnaires assessing physical activity, perceived social support, self-esteem, depressive symptoms, and life satisfaction.

The primary objective was to examine whether perceived social support and self-esteem functioned as individual and sequential mediators in the associations between physical activity and mental health outcomes. Life satisfaction and depressive symptoms were evaluated as separate outcome variables.

Statistical analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics version 24 and the PROCESS macro version 4.0. Serial mediation analysis was employed to examine direct and indirect statistical associations between physical activity and the selected mental health indicators.

As an observational study, no intervention was administered, and the cross-sectional design was intended to assess associations rather than establish causal relationships.
primary_outcomes: Life Satisfaction Score
title: The Mediating Role of Social Support and Self-Esteem in the Effect of Physical Activity on the Mental Health of University Students

brief_summary:
Objective: To investigate the application effect of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) fumigation nursing intervention in uremic patients with refractory skin pruritus undergoing hemoperfusion treatment.

Methods: A total of 68 uremic patients with refractory skin pruritus admitted to the Department of Nephrology of a large hospital in Jiangxi, China, between May 2026 and May 2027 were enrolled as study subjects. All patients received routine hemodialysis combined with hemoperfusion treatment as prescribed by physicians. They were divided into a control group (n = 34) and an experimental group (n = 34) using a random number table method. The control group received routine nursing care, while the experimental group received additional TCM fumigation nursing intervention on the basis of the control group. The Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) score, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) score, 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) score, and blood biochemical indicators (serum calcium, serum phosphorus, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) were compared between the two groups before intervention and after 8 weeks of intervention.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University
primary_outcomes: Pruritus severity was assessed using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS)
title: TCM Fumigation Care for Uremic Refractory Pruritus During Hemoperfusion

brief_summary: The aim of this randomised, double-blind, controlled experimental study is to investigate the effect of Sufi music delivered via a bone-conduction pillow speaker on sleep quality, cardiac symptoms and vital signs in open-heart surgery patients. The study will be conducted with three groups, each comprising 30 patients (90 in total): an intervention group, a sham group and a routine care control group. Participants in the intervention group will listen to relaxing Sufi music without percussion for 15-20 minutes, starting at 21:30, through a bone-conduction pillow speaker placed under the pillow. Participants in the sham group will have an identical-looking pillow speaker placed under their pillow for the same duration, but no sound will be transmitted. Participants in the control group will receive only the hospital's standard night-care protocol, with no device or music intervention. Vital signs (blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate and oxygen saturation) will be measured immediately before and after the application period in all groups, and sleep quality will be assessed the following morning between 08:00 and 09:00 using the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire. Cardiac symptoms will be assessed in all groups with a Cardiac Symptom Survey before discharge.
primary_outcomes: Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire
title: Effect of Sufi Music on Sleep, Cardiac Symptoms and Vital Signs in Open-Heart Surgery Patients

brief_summary:

Does daily, weekly, and on-demand doxycycline dosing strategies lower the incidence of quarterly STIs (gonorrhea, chlamydia, and syphilis)?

Complete text surveys once every month
primary_outcomes: Quarterly incidence of chlamydia, gonorrhea, and/or early syphilis infection

brief_summary:
This is an observational cohort study. Investigators do not assign any intervention to participants. Chemotherapy was received in a completed clinical trial or is determined by the treating physicians as part of routine care, and study results will not be used to guide treatment.

The study aims to identify clinicopathological and molecular features associated with outcomes after anthracycline-free or anthracycline-containing chemotherapy in women with high-risk, HER2-negative early breast cancer. Existing clinical and follow-up data and archived tumor tissue from participants of a trial completed at Peking Union Medical College Hospital (NCT01354522; enrollment ended in 2013) will be analyzed with gene expression, metabolic, and digital pathology methods to develop a prediction model. Tumor tissue remaining after routine surgery or biopsy will also be collected, with informed consent, from up to 50 additional patients for single-cell sequencing. All analyses are exploratory.

brief_summary:
Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a blood cancer with a substantial risk of relapse after initial treatment. Although patients with favorable-risk AML generally have better outcomes, relapse remains a major concern. Interferon-alpha (IFN-α) may help prevent relapse, but its effectiveness as maintenance therapy has not been confirmed in prospective studies.

This prospective, single-arm study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of IFN-α as maintenance therapy in patients with favorable-risk AML. Participants will receive IFN-α maintenance treatment and will be followed for disease relapse, survival, and treatment-related adverse events.

brief_summary:
Breastfeeding difficulties may affect both infants and mothers, particularly following instrumental vaginal delivery using forceps or vacuum extraction. Some infants may experience restricted neck movement or muscle tension that could interfere with positioning, attachment to the breast, and effective breastfeeding. Mothers may also experience pain during feeding.

This clinical trial aims to determine whether adding manual physiotherapy to conventional breastfeeding support improves breastfeeding performance in infants born following instrumental vaginal delivery.

The study will include 126 mother-infant pairs experiencing breastfeeding difficulties. Eligible infants must have been born at term, be no older than three months at enrollment, and have been delivered using forceps or vacuum extraction.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will receive conventional breastfeeding guidance and a home exercise program. In addition, infants in the experimental group will receive six sessions of gentle manual physiotherapy, approximately once a week. Infants in the control group will not receive the study-specific manual physiotherapy treatment.

Breastfeeding performance will be assessed using the Bristol Breastfeeding Assessment Tool (BBAT), which evaluates infant positioning, attachment, sucking, and swallowing. The study will also assess infant neck movement, maternal pain during breastfeeding, and infant irritability.

Assessments will take place at the beginning of the study (Day 0), on Days 15 and 30, at the end of the treatment period (Day 37), and when the infant reaches six months of age. The main comparison between the two groups will be the change in breastfeeding performance from Day 0 to Day 37.

The study hypothesis is that infants receiving manual physiotherapy in addition to conventional breastfeeding support will show greater improvement in breastfeeding performance than infants receiving conventional support alone.

The results may help determine whether manual physiotherapy is a useful complementary treatment for breastfeeding difficulties following instrumental vaginal delivery.
interventions: Conventional Breastfeeding Support and Home Exercises
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Bristol Breastfeeding Assessment Tool. Total Score at Day 37
Change from Baseline in Infant Cervical Range of Motion at Day 37
Change from Baseline in Maternal Breastfeeding Pain Assessed by the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at Day 37
title: Effectiveness of Physiotherapy Interventions in the Management of Breastfeeding Difficulties After Instrumental Births: A Clinical Study

brief_summary: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB) is an inherited mucocutaneous fragility disorder caused by pathogenic variants in COL7A1, leading to blistering, scarring, and significant morbidity. Pruritus is a major complication that substantially impairs patients' quality of life, yet effective treatment options remain limited. Nemolizumab, an interleukin-31 receptor alpha antagonist, inhibits IL-31 signaling, a pathway potentially involved in DEB-associated pruritus. Elevated IL-31 levels have been reported in patients with recessive DEB (RDEB) and correlated with pruritus severity, supporting its potential role as a therapeutic target. We hypothesize that nemolizumab may represent an effective and safe treatment option for pruritus in patients with DEB.
primary_outcomes: To study the efficacy of Nemolizumab on pruritus in patients > 12yo with DEB after 4 weeks of treatment, in a multicentric, prospective, and open pilot study.

brief_summary:
Stroke is a leading cause of death and adult disability. Stroke care is still limited by fragmented care pathways, non-standardised diagnostic work-up and follow-up, and local, non-interoperable data systems across the pre-hospital, in-hospital and post-hospital settings.

UMBRELLA-P is a multicentre, prospective, observational study in 7 university hospitals in 6 European countries (Spain, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland). Adults with clinically suspected acute stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) are managed according to standard of care. Routine clinical, imaging, laboratory, ECG and patient-reported data are collected, pseudonymised, stored on a dedicated server at each hospital and harmonised to the OMOP Common Data Model.

The harmonised data form a federated real-world data platform (U-Platform). On this platform, artificial intelligence (AI) models are trained and validated through federated learning, so that no patient data leave the participating sites. The models aim to predict short- and long-term outcomes, reduce time to treatment, and support diagnosis, triage, discharge, follow-up and secondary prevention. Five clinical sub-studies address pre-hospital triage, fast track to reperfusion, emergent intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) management, TIA/minor stroke, and cardiac evaluation with blood biomarkers.

The study is observational. The outputs of the AI models are used for research only and will not influence clinical decisions. Participants are followed for up to 12 months.
lead_sponsor: Hospital Universitari Vall d'Hebron Research Institute
primary_outcomes: Area Under the Curve (AUC) of the Pre-hospital AI Model for Detection of Large Vessel Occlusion (LVO) Stroke (WP2)
AUC of the Image-based AI Tool for Prediction of Successful Reperfusion After Endovascular Thrombectomy (WP3)
AUC of the AI Model for Prediction of Early Hematoma Expansion in Intracerebral Hemorrhage (WP4)
C-statistic of the AI Risk Model for Prediction of Recurrent Stroke After TIA or Minor Stroke (WP5)
AUC of the Multimodal AI Tool for Identification of a Cardio-aortic Source of Embolism (WP6)
title: AI-Based Tools for Stroke Diagnosis, Treatment and Outcome Prediction: a Multicentre Prospective Observational Study

Methods: A total of 40 patients (regardless patients sex) with an age ranged from 9 to 12 years with class Ⅱ Div1 mal-occlusion and class 2 skeletal pattern will be included in the study.

brief_summary:
Male hypogonadism is a chronic endocrine condition characterized by deficient testosterone production, leading to adverse changes in body composition (decreased lean mass, increased fat mass) and various physical and psychological symptoms, including fatigue and reduced motivation. Although testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is the primary medical treatment, its effectiveness in optimizing body composition largely depends on regular physical activity. However, the psychosocial mechanisms underlying exercise engagement in this specific population remain insufficiently explored.

Exercise self-efficacy, an individual's confidence in their ability to perform physical activity, is a major determinant of exercise behavior. While its mediating role between body composition and physical activity has been shown in other clinical populations, it has not been investigated in men with hypogonadism, where low testosterone levels uniquely impair psychological well-being and drive.

The primary objective of this cross-sectional study is to evaluate the mediating role of exercise self-efficacy in the relationship between body composition and physical activity levels in men with hypogonadism receiving TRT. Additionally, the study explores the potential moderating effects of serum total testosterone levels and TRT duration, while controlling for depressive symptoms as a covariate. Findings from this study aim to provide evidence-based guidance for clinicians and physical therapists in designing targeted exercise interventions and timing rehabilitation strategies for hypogonadal patients.
primary_outcomes: Physical Activity Level
title: Exercise Self-Efficacy, Body Composition, and Physical Activity in Men With Hypogonadism

brief_summary: Type 2 diabetes needs daily self-management, but most of it happens outside the clinic, where patients get little continuous support. This randomized controlled trial will test an Arabic-language mobile application with an artificial intelligence chatbot for adults with type 2 diabetes attending outpatient diabetes clinics in Egypt. The application offers diabetes education, reminders, glucose and activity logging, goal setting, prompts that adapt when use declines, a diabetes distress check, and nurse oversight. A total of 120 adults will be randomly assigned equally to usual care plus the application for 8 weeks, or to usual care with an educational leaflet. Outcome assessors will not know group assignment. The main outcome is self-efficacy. Other outcomes are self-care behaviors, medication adherence, disease knowledge, random blood glucose, diabetes distress, and application use, measured at the start, at 8 weeks, and 6 and 12 weeks after the intervention ends. About 20 intervention participants will then be interviewed about their experiences and what helps or hinders continued use, and these findings will be combined with the trial results.

brief_summary:
This study is evaluating MR-guided Focused Ultrasound (MRgFUS) treatment for people with Parkinson's disease (PD) who have disabling tremor, bradykinesia, and rigidity despite optimal medical therapy.

The study uses the Exablate Neuro System, which delivers ultrasound energy on a specific brain target and generates a small lesion (ablation) without making a surgical incision.

This study evaluates three treatment approaches targeting different brain structures involved in Parkinson's motor symptoms:

* Pallidothalamic Tractotomy (PTT): targeting pathways connecting the globus pallidus to the thalamus and subthalamic region structures.
* Thalamotomy (VIM): targeting the ventral intermediate nucleus of the thalamus, a structure involved in pathogenesis of tremor.
* Combined PTT+VIM: targeting both structures during a single treatment procedure.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups: PTT, VIM, PTT+VIM, or "delayed treatment". Participants in the delayed-treatment group will continue best medical therapy for 6 months before receiving MRgFUS treatment.

The study aims to determine whether PTT provides greater improvement in motor symptoms than optimized medical therapy alone, whether adding VIM treatment to PTT improves tremor control, and whether adding PTT to VIM treatment provides additional improvement in bradykinesia and rigidity.

The main outcome measures are changes in the MDS-UPDRS Part III motor scores:

1. Overall motor symptoms: change in the contralateral body-side MDS-UPDRS Part III motor score at 6 months after randomization, comparing PTT with delayed treatment.
2. Tremor: change in the contralateral tremor score at 6, 12 months after treatment, comparing PTT+VIM with PTT alone.
3. Bradykinesia and rigidity: change in the contralateral bradykinesia and rigidity score at 6, 12 months after treatment, comparing PTT+VIM with VIM alone.

MDS-UPDRS Part III is a standard clinical scale used to assess Parkinson's motor symptoms. Assessments are performed in the OFF-medication state, meaning Parkinson's medications are temporarily withheld to better evaluate the treatment effect.

In addition, changes in motor complications, tremor severity, quality of life, and medication requirements will be assessed using MDS-UPDRS Parts II-IV, the Clinical Rating Scale for Tremor (CRST), the Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire (PDQ-39), and levodopa equivalent daily dose (LEDD).

Treatment-related adverse events, cognitive function, and ablation spot characteristics will also be evaluated throughout follow-up.

brief_summary:
Problem. Helicobacter pylori infection is the most prevalent bacterial infection in humans and the main modifiable risk factor for gastric adenocarcinoma. In Uruguay, where clarithromycin resistance is either unknown or above 15% and neither bismuth nor tetracyclines are available, the first-line regimen is non-bismuth quadruple (concomitant) therapy with omeprazole, clarithromycin, amoxicillin and metronidazole (OCAM) for 14 days. Its main limitation is tolerability: adverse events affect up to 40% of patients and account for discontinuation rates of 2-10%, and the regimen exerts selective pressure through four simultaneous drugs.

Research question. In adult patients with H. pylori infection and an indication for eradication treated at tertiary care centers in Uruguay, does dual therapy with vonoprazan and amoxicillin for 14 days reduce the frequency and severity of adverse events compared with non-bismuth concomitant quadruple therapy (OCAM) for 14 days? Primary objective. To compare the frequency and severity of adverse events between both eradication regimens.

Design. Randomized, experimental, prospective, multicenter (4 centers), triple-blinded clinical trial (treating physician, research team and statistician). Reported in accordance with the CONSORT statement.

Population. Patients aged 18 to 75 years with H. pylori infection confirmed by histology, rapid urease test, stool antigen test, serology or urea breath test, with an indication for eradication according to the Maastricht VI/Florence consensus, treated at Hospital de Clínicas, Asistencial Médica-Sanatorio Cantegril, DNSP and COMEPA.

Intervention. Group A: vonoprazan 20 mg every 12 hours plus amoxicillin 1 g every 8 hours for 14 days. Group B: omeprazole 20 mg, clarithromycin 500 mg, metronidazole 500 mg and amoxicillin 1 g, all every 12 hours for 14 days.

Primary endpoint. Maximum adverse event severity per participant, an ordinal variable with four categories (absent, mild, moderate, severe) according to CTCAE v5.0, collected through a self-administered questionnaire at the end of treatment.

Secondary endpoints. Eradication rate, confirmed at least 45 days after treatment initiation; treatment adherence (intake of ≥80% of the prescribed regimen); number of distinct symptoms and duration in days per participant.

Sample size and analysis. Fifty participants per group. Bivariate comparisons were performed with the chi-square test or Fisher exact test, and ordinal logistic regression was applied with assessment of the proportional odds assumption (Brant test), in Stata 18.0.

Keywords: Helicobacter pylori; Vonoprazan; Amoxicillin; Dual therapy; Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions; Randomized Controlled Trial; Uruguay.
primary_outcomes: Maximum severity of adverse events per participant
title: Safety of Vonoprazan-Amoxicillin Dual Therapy Versus Concomitant Quadruple Therapy for H. Pylori Eradication

brief_summary:
Intermittent hemodialysis (IHD) is the first-line kidney replacement modality in 50% of severe acute kidney injury (AKI) cases in French intensive care units (ICUs). It clears uremic toxins and restores acid-base and fluid-sodium balance, but the osmotic imbalance it induces can cause or worsen hemodynamic and neurological failure. Dialysis dose is a major prognostic issue, yet the optimal target and the best tools to quantify it in AKI remain debated.

Kt/Vd, validated in chronic kidney disease, is largely biased in AKI because the urea distribution volume is altered by fluid overload, capillary hyperpermeability and impaired tissue perfusion. Alternatives include the urea reduction ratio (URR) and the solute removal index (SRI), simple measures that each require only one additional sample, but their relevance for guiding IHD strategy remains to be demonstrated. Kt alone is considered reliable in AKI, as urea clearance measured by ionic dialysance has been validated in the ICU, but neither Kt nor Kt indexed to body weight or body surface area has been evaluated in clinical practice.

Current recommendations set a minimum dose of three 4-hour sessions per week, with a blood flow \> 200 mL/min and a dialysate flow \> 500 mL/min. This target standardizes care and simplifies planning, but the lack of personalization and of session quality measurement may lead to an inadequate dose in some patients.

AIKIDDO is an observational study of 200 adult ICU patients with KDIGO stage 3 AKI treated with IHD. It aims to assess the agreement between dialysis dose measures (Kt/Vd, double-pool Kt/Vd, Kt, URR, SRI) obtained at each dialysis session. Patients are followed until Day 29 for death, dialysis dependence, renal recovery, neurological status, hemodynamic instability during sessions and duration of invasive mechanical ventilation.

Kt/Vd: Kt divided by the patient's urea distribution volume (Vd, L)
Double-pool Kt/Vd: Kt/Vd calculated with a double-pool urea kinetic model
URR: urea reduction ratio, based on post-dialysis plasma urea
SRI: solute removal index, based on urea in the effluent
title: Acute Kidney Injury and Intermittent Dialysis Dose

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate the effects of a 12-week wearable-monitored workplace exercise program on physical performance, brain activity, and biological markers in office workers.

Prolonged sitting is common among office workers and may negatively affect physical health and well-being. This study will examine whether incorporating regular, technology-assisted exercise breaks into the workday can improve physical performance and produce measurable changes in brain activity and proteins found in blood and sweat.

A total of 78 Thai office workers aged 20-59 years will participate in this study. Participants will be classified according to their habitual physical activity levels into active and sedentary office workers. The 26 active office workers will continue their usual physical activity habits and serve as an active control group. The 52 sedentary office workers will be randomly allocated into two groups: a self-monitoring control group (26 participants) and an experimental group (26 participants).

The self-monitoring control group will receive educational information about the health benefits of reducing prolonged sitting and will use a logbook to monitor their sitting behaviors while maintaining their usual daily routines. The experimental group will participate in a 12-week wearable-monitored workplace exercise program using an intelligent wearable device and a gamified smartphone application. The system provides exercise prompts, real-time feedback, and personalized guidance to encourage participants to perform short exercise sessions during their workday, with a target of at least 150 minutes of exercise per week.

All participants will undergo assessments before and after the intervention. These assessments will evaluate physical performance, muscle strength, movement characteristics, cortical excitability and inhibition using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), and biological markers obtained from blood and sweat samples. Additional assessments will include body composition, physical activity levels, musculoskeletal discomfort, and the usability and acceptability of the exercise system.

The study will compare changes in these measurements among the three groups to determine the effects of the wearable-monitored workplace exercise program and explore its potential benefits for improving physical performance, neurological function, and exercise-related biological responses in office workers.

Exploratory analyses will investigate treatment-associated changes in leukemic cell differentiation and apoptosis and identify potential biomarkers associated with treatment response.

Aim: To assess intratendinous pressure in individuals with and without midportion Achilles tendinopathy and investigate its correlation with tendon structure, patient characteristics, and pain symptoms.

brief_summary:
The goal of this multicenter observational study is to develop and validate an artificial intelligence-based digital pathology model to predict treatment response and prognosis in adult men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with androgen deprivation therapy plus androgen receptor signaling inhibitors.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can digital pathology-based artificial intelligence predict deep prostate-specific antigen response, defined as prostate-specific antigen less than 0.2 ng/mL at 6 to 7 months after treatment? Can digital pathology-based artificial intelligence predict progression to metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and time to metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer? Researchers will compare artificial intelligence-defined low-risk and high-risk groups to evaluate whether the model can improve prediction of treatment response and prognosis beyond conventional clinicopathological risk stratification.

Participants will not receive any additional intervention as part of this study. Researchers will retrospectively collect clinical characteristics, treatment records, prostate-specific antigen response data, follow-up outcomes, and archived prostate biopsy slides from participating centers. brief_summary:
In July 2026 the electrophysiology laboratory of a Czech tertiary cardiology centre introduced topical cyanoacrylate tissue adhesive (DERMABOND Mini or Histoacryl) as a routine alternative to the figure-of-eight suture for closing femoral venous puncture sites after electrophysiology procedures, including pulsed-field ablation performed through 13-17 F sheaths. After sheath removal, haemostasis is achieved by manual compression and the adhesive seals the skin over the puncture. The change was a clinical decision of the department, not a study intervention.

Published experience with this approach is limited, particularly for large-bore venous sheaths. GLUE-EP evaluates the access-site safety of the practice change using routinely recorded data only. Procedures closed with tissue adhesive are compared with a historical cohort closed with a figure-of-eight suture in 2024-2025 (propensity-score matched) and with a concurrent cohort closed with a suture during the same period. A prospective continuation collects the same routine data until 30 June 2027 from patients who give written informed consent.

The study assigns no treatment, adds no examination, questionnaire or study visit, and does not influence how the puncture site is closed. The primary outcome is any major or minor access-site vascular complication within 30 days of the procedure.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Access-Site Vascular Complications
title: Tissue Adhesive Versus Figure-of-Eight Suture for Femoral Venous Closure After Electrophysiology Procedures (GLUE-EP)

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does neuromuscular taping, applied once a week for 3 weeks in addition to standard exercise therapy, reduce muscle pain more than placebo taping?

Researchers will compare neuromuscular taping applied with a muscle and fascial technique to placebo taping (the same tape placed on the same area without tension or therapeutic technique) to see if the active taping provides greater pain relief.

brief_summary: Piriformis syndrome is a neuromuscular disorder causing buttock pain and sciatic nerve irritation, leading to functional limitations. This study aims to compare the effectiveness of two manual therapy techniques-Strain Counterstrain (SCS) and Active Release Technique (ART)-on pain, functional disability, and hip range of motion in patients with piriformis syndrome. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will receive a baseline treatment of a hot pack and Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS). The SCS group will additionally receive the strain counterstrain technique, while the ART group will receive the active release technique. Treatment will be administered three times per week for four weeks. Outcomes will be measured using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS), and a goniometer for range of motion, assessed at baseline and after four weeks.

brief_summary:
Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) is defined as "flow outside of normal volume, duration, regularity, or frequency". Acute AUB is excessive bleeding that requires immediate intervention to prevent further blood loss. Chronic AUB refers to irregularities in menstrual bleeding for most of the previous 6 months.

AUB can be frequent or infrequent, prolonged, irregular, or heavy. Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) is defined as "excessive menstrual blood loss which interferes with a woman's physical, social, emotional and/or material quality of life". Causes of AUB are classified as polyps, adenomyosis, leiomyomas (AUB-L), malignancy and premalignant conditions, coagulopathy, ovulatory disorders (AUB-O), endometrial disorders (AUB-E), iatrogenic, and 'not classified ' . AUB affects approximately one in four women between 30 and 50 years of age, with serious implications on woman's quality of life (QoL). Endometrial ablation (EA) is a uterus-preserving procedure that aims to destroy or remove the endometrial tissue in selected women who have no desire for future fertility. EA has become an alternative to hysterectomy in the treatment of AUB because it is less invasive and has a shorter recovery period. At present, many different techniques are available to remove the endometrial tissue. Resectoscopic endometrial ablation (REA) consists of targeted endometrial destruction under direct hysteroscopic visualization. REA techniques include endometrial laser ablation, transcervical resection of the endometrium, and rollerball endometrial ablation. Non-resectoscopic endometrial ablation (NREA) uses a variety of energy sources to non-selectively destroy the endometrial lining and include thermal balloon endometrial ablation, microwave endometrial ablation, hydrothermal ablation, bipolar radiofrequency endometrial ablation, endometrial cryotherapy, and more recently vapor endometrial ablation. NREA technologies require short surgical time and can also be performed in the outpatient setting. Vapor EA is one of the newest approaches in the field. In this context, the Aqua Therapeutics Thermal Therapy Vapor Ablation system (ATTTVAS; AQUA Therapeutics Inc.) is a novel system designed to ablate uterine tissue using vapor thermal therapy technology. The ATTTVAS is indicated to ablate the endometrial lining of the uterus in premenopausal women with abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) due to benign causes for whom childbearing is complete. In this Pre-Market, Traditional Feasibility, Pilot, Interventional, Clinical Investigation we aim to evaluate the Safety and the Performance of the Aqua Therapeutics Thermal Therapy Vapor Ablation System (ATTTVAS) In Premenopausal Women with Abnormal Uterine Bleeding (AUB) and a History of Cesarean Section.

brief_summary: This retrospective observational multicenter study aims to describe the management of acute pain in children with sickle cell disease treated in the emergency departments of the University Hospitals of Nancy, Strasbourg, and Reims, France. The study analyzed routinely collected medical data from pediatric patients presenting with acute painful episodes related to sickle cell disease. Information regarding pain assessment, analgesic treatment, timing of care, and clinical outcomes was reviewed. No additional procedures or interventions were performed for the purpose of this study. All data were collected as part of standard clinical care. The results of this study may help improve the management of acute pain in children with sickle cell disease in emergency settings.

brief_summary:
The overall goal of this study is to inform the design and establish feasibility for a future clinical trial to determine the optimal management of women living with HIV (WLWH) with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) detected on HPV-based cervical cancer screening. WLWH have a higher diversity of anogenital HPV types causing cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (hHSIL) and invasive cancer compared to women without HIV. While there is consensus that women testing positive for HPV 16 and/or 18 should be immediately managed and treated, optimal management strategies for women with other hrHPV types (non-16/18) are not well defined.

This prospective cohort study will enroll WLWH undergoing cervical cancer screening using primary HPV testing. Women will self-collect vaginal specimens for hrHPV testing using the Abbott Alinity m HPV assay, which provides extended HPV genotyping and a proxy for HPV viral load based on cycle threshold (CT) values. Women with hrHPV detected will return for further evaluation and treatment as indicated. A subset of women will return at Month 6 for repeat evaluation.

The study will evaluate feasibility for a future trial by examining recruitment, retention, return for evaluation, and completion of treatment. It will also explore management strategies for women with non-16/18 hrHPV based on extended genotyping and HPV viral load compared to standard of care approaches using visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA).

brief_summary:
Patients who need a breathing machine (ventilator) for a long time are often considered for a tracheostomy, a surgical opening in the front of the neck through which a breathing tube is placed. Because most of these patients cannot speak for themselves, family members are usually asked to make this decision on their behalf, often with limited information, high uncertainty, and common misconceptions about what life after tracheostomy will be like. Patient decision aids are tools that explain the options, their benefits and downsides, and help people think about what matters most to them.

The investigators have developed a short animated video decision aid about tracheostomy for families in Taiwan, with Mandarin narration and subtitles and a Taiwanese local-language version. This study will test whether the animated video helps family members more than a printed booklet that contains exactly the same information.

Adult family decision-makers of ventilated patients in the Respiratory Care Center of National Taiwan University Hospital Hsin-Chu Branch whose care team is considering a tracheostomy will be invited to take part. After answering baseline questions, participants will be randomly assigned, to either watch the animated video (about 8 to 10 minutes on a tablet) or read the printed booklet (about 8 to 10 minutes). A trained nurse will then go over the key points with them in the same way for both groups, and participants will complete a questionnaire right away. Everything takes place in a single visit, and usual care and family meetings with the care team continue as normal.

The main question is whether family members who watch the animated video will know more about tracheostomy immediately afterward than those who read the booklet. The study will also compare how prepared family members feel to make the decision, what they value most when weighing the two options, and how anxious they feel. The investigators hypothesize that the animated decision aid will lead to higher tracheostomy knowledge scores and greater preparation for decision making than the paper booklet.
primary_outcomes: Tracheostomy Knowledge Score
title: Animated Versus Paper-Based Patient Decision Aids for Tracheostomy: Effects on Family Caregivers' Knowledge and Preparation for Decision Making-A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This study aimed to assess the nutritional status of children under five years of age, identify factors associated with malnutrition, and evaluate the effects of a community-based nutrition intervention guided by family medicine principles in two communes of Bac Me District, Ha Giang Province, Vietnam.

The study employed a non-randomized controlled community intervention design. Yen Cuong commune was assigned to the intervention group, while Phieng Luong commune served as the comparison group.

The intervention included maternal nutrition education, individualized counseling, practical feeding demonstrations, growth monitoring, home visits, and coordinated family- and community-oriented care. The comparison group continued to receive routine child healthcare and nutrition services.

Assessments were conducted at baseline and approximately 6, 12, and 15 months after the start of the intervention. The study evaluated maternal nutrition knowledge and feeding practices, dietary intake, childhood illnesses, anthropometric indicators, and nutritional status.

The study was conducted from July 2024 to November 2025 and was completed before its retrospective registration on ClinicalTrials.gov.
interventions: Family Medicine-Oriented Nutrition Education and Counseling

primary_outcomes: Change in the Prevalence of Overall Undernutrition
title: Effectiveness of a Family Medicine-Oriented Community Nutrition Intervention on Child Growth and Feeding Practices in Northern Vietnam

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a strong magnet (neodymium magnet) can help doctors remove metal objects stuck under the skin in adults. It will also learn about the safety of this method. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How often can doctors remove the metal object with the help of the magnet?
* How long does the procedure take?
* How often do doctors need to make a cut in the skin, and how long is the cut?
* What problems do participants have within 15 days after the procedure?
* How satisfied are participants with the procedure?

Participants will:

* Have an X-ray to find the metal object
* Have the metal object removed with the help of the magnet in the emergency department, with or without numbing medicine (local anesthetic)
* Come back for a wound check 15 days after the procedure
primary_outcomes: Successful removal of the foreign body
title: Neodymium Magnet-Guided Removal of Metallic Soft Tissue Foreign Bodies in the Emergency Department

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn which level of adductor canal block (proximal, mid, or distal) gives the best pain relief after total knee replacement while preserving leg muscle strength. The study includes adults aged 18-75 having knee replacement under spinal anesthesia.

The main question is: Does the block level change how much opioid (tramadol) patients need in the first 24 hours after surgery?

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups and receive an ultrasound-guided block with 30 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine before surgery. Pain, opioid use, numbness, muscle function, walking ability, side effects, and recovery quality will be assessed for 48 hours after surgery.
primary_outcomes: Total Tramadol Consumption in the First 24 Hours
title: Proximal, Mid, and Distal Adductor Canal Block for Pain Control After Total Knee Arthroplasty

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study will evaluate the effect of intravenous dexamethasone on postoperative analgesia in children undergoing hip surgery with a pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block.

A total of 90 participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive intravenous placebo, dexamethasone 0.1 mg/kg, or dexamethasone 0.2 mg/kg. All participants will receive a PENG block as part of standardized multimodal postoperative analgesia.

The primary outcome will be cumulative intravenous nalbuphine consumption, expressed as mg/kg, during the first 48 hours after surgery. Secondary outcomes will include time to first rescue nalbuphine administration, postoperative pain intensity, the proportion of participants requiring rescue opioid analgesia, postoperative nausea and vomiting, blood glucose levels, and adverse events.

The study aims to determine whether intravenous dexamethasone reduces postoperative opioid requirements after PENG block and whether the analgesic effect differs between the two studied dexamethasone doses.
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Intravenous Nalbuphine Consumption
title: Intravenous Dexamethasone for PENG Block Analgesia in Children Undergoing Hip Surgery

brief_summary:
Diabetic macular edema (DME) is a complication of diabetes that causes fluid accumulation in the central retina, potentially leading to impaired vision. Intravitreal injections of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) medications, including ranibizumab and aflibercept, are commonly used to treat this condition.

This prospective, randomized, comparative study aimed to evaluate and compare the effects of intravitreal ranibizumab and aflibercept on macular vascular density in patients with diabetic macular edema using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), a noninvasive imaging technique that visualizes retinal blood vessels.

The study included 80 eyes with diabetic macular edema, randomly assigned to two equal treatment groups. One group received ranibizumab, while the other received aflibercept. Each eye received three intravitreal injections. Changes in retinal vascular density, central retinal thickness, and visual acuity were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months.

The study aimed to determine whether OCTA measurements could help evaluate treatment response and identify vascular changes associated with improvement in diabetic macular edema.
primary_outcomes: Change in Macular Vascular Density Assessed by Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography
title: Macular Vascular Density After Aflibercept or Ranibizumab Treatment for Diabetic Macular Edema

brief_summary:
This multicenter, randomized, open-label, exploratory phase II study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of perioperative Retlirafusp Alfa plus SOX versus adebrelimab plus SOX in adult patients with previously untreated, HER2-negative, resectable locally advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (clinical stage II-III, AJCC 8th edition).

Approximately 98 participants will be randomized at a 1:1 ratio via stratified block randomization. Stratification factors include tumor location (gastric versus gastroesophageal junction) and PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS \<1 versus CPS ≥1).

Participants will receive 3 preoperative cycles of assigned immunotherapy combined with SOX, followed by D2 radical gastrectomy performed 4-8 weeks after the last neoadjuvant cycle. Postoperatively, participants will receive 5 cycles of the same immunotherapy plus SOX, then up to 9 cycles of immunotherapy monotherapy, with a maximum of 17 total immunotherapy cycles.

The primary outcome measure is pathologic complete response (pCR) rate. Secondary outcome measures include R0 resection rate, event-free survival, disease-free survival, overall survival, surgical safety, adverse events, laboratory abnormalities, and treatment tolerability.
primary_outcomes: Pathologic Complete Response (pCR) Rate

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether a non-invasive electromagnetic wave scanner (EDE CARDIO BIO-MAP) can help diagnose myocardial infarction (heart attack) in adults (18 years and older) who come to the emergency department with chest pain and suspected myocardial infarction. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How sensitive and specific is the EDE scanner in diagnosing myocardial infarction (MI) compared with standard blood tests (e.g., cardiac troponin)?
* How sensitive and specific are the immediate blood measurements from a portable lab device compared with conventional hospital laboratory measurements? Researchers will compare the results of the EDE scanner and the portable lab with standard hospital blood test results and the final clinical diagnosis to see how accurately each detects MI.

Participants will:

* Have a research visit (30 minutes to 1 hour) during their emergency care, including a quick scan with the Exponential Deep Examination (EDE) device (attached to a phone or tablet) and a small research blood sample tested on a portable lab device
* Repeat the scan and blood sample 4 to 6 hours later, only if a second blood draw is already needed for their clinical care
* Answer questions about their medical and social history, and allow the study team to collect relevant results from their medical record Scanner results will not be shared with participants or used for their clinical care.

Participants will have their symptoms (such as pain, tiredness, nausea, or shortness of breath) and their level of diagnostic and therapeutic intensity assessed within the first 72 hours of admission, as part of routine care. brief_summary:
This is a single-arm clinical trial to evaluate the PK profile in breast milk and plasma after a single oral dose of zoliflodacin in healthy lactating women.

Eligible participants who have been actively breastfeeding or expressing milk for at least 4 weeks postpartum will receive a single dose of zoliflodacin administered as an oral suspension with food.

Breast milk and plasma samples will be collected at predefined time points for up to 48 hours after dosing to characterize zoliflodacin concentrations and estimate drug exposure in breast milk and maternal plasma. Participants will temporarily discontinue breastfeeding from study check-in until 72 hours after dosing to avoid infant exposure to zoliflodacin. Breast milk will be expressed using an electronic breast pump and collected according to the study schedule.

Participants will be admitted to the clinical research unit the day before dosing and discharged after completion of the 48-hour PK sampling period. A follow-up visit will be conducted approximately 7 days after dosing to assess safety and tolerability. A lactation consultant will be available throughout the study period and for up to 30 days after dosing, as needed.

brief_summary:
Recovery from substance use disorders (SUD) unfolds within individual, interpersonal and environmental contexts. In therapeutic communities, social support, participation and community climate may be part of the pathway through which psychological change relates to functioning during treatment. This prospective, observational, longitudinal cohort study of people in residential SUD treatment will test a sequential mediation model in which helplessness precedes behavioral avoidance, avoidance is related to lower environmental reward, and lower environmental reward is in turn associated with more frequent negative automatic thoughts.

The study will also examine whether community context modifies the association between avoidance and environmental reward, and whether psychological flexibility is independently associated with environmental reward and negative automatic thoughts.

Participants will be assessed weekly during residential treatment with validated self-report instruments and periodic written narratives. Repeated observations are nested within participants and are analyzed with multilevel models that separate within-person from between-person effects, using prespecified time lags (helplessness at time t, avoidance at t+1, environmental reward at t+2, negative automatic thoughts at t+3). No intervention is assigned and the community context is not manipulated.
interventions: Routine residential therapeutic community treatment (not assigned by the study)
primary_outcomes: Sequential indirect effect of helplessness on negative automatic thoughts through avoidance and environmental reward (IE = a1 × a2 × b)
title: Community Context and Psychological Flexibility in Residential Substance Use Treatment: A Longitudinal Sequential Mediation Study

brief_summary:
Relative motion flexion (RMF) orthoses are used in hand rehabilitation to position finger joints in a controlled degree of flexion. These orthoses are traditionally made from low-temperature thermoplastic materials. Three-dimensional (3D) printing offers an alternative method of producing individually designed orthoses using different filament materials.

The purpose of this study was to compare finger joint stabilization and user satisfaction among RMF orthoses made from two 3D-printing materials, thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) and polylactic acid (PLA), and a conventional low-temperature thermoplastic (LTT) material.

The study included 30 healthy adult volunteers. Each participant used all three types of RMF orthoses for two consecutive days per orthosis, with the order of application randomly determined. The orthoses were designed to position the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint at 30 degrees of flexion.

Joint positioning was evaluated using a goniometer, and user satisfaction was assessed using the Quebec User Evaluation of Satisfaction with Assistive Technology (QUEST 2.0).

The study aimed to provide comparative information about orthosis materials and fabrication methods that may help guide future orthotic applications in hand rehabilitation.
interventions: Low-Temperature Thermoplastic Relative Motion Flexion Orthosis
primary_outcomes: MCP Joint Stabilization
title: 3D Versus Low-Temperature Thermoplastic Relative Motion Orthosis: MP Joint Stabilization

brief_summary:
Physiotherapy is essential for patients suffering from chronic muscle diseases or nerve damage. These conditions often reduce hand strength and dexterity, which significantly impacts daily quality of life. Since travelling to in-person therapy can be difficult due to mobility issues, this project provides a home-based, small-group hand training program guided live by a physiotherapist via an online video platform (such as Google Meet).

The study uses a cross-over design. After initial assessments, patients are randomly split into two groups that take turns participating in a 12-week exercise program. The online sessions take place three times a week for one hour, with patients sitting at a table at home. The physiotherapist is present online to provide real-time feedback and interact with the participants.

In-person health assessments are conducted at the Department of Neurology, University of Pécs. These check-ups take place at the very beginning, right before and after the 12-week training period, and during a 3-month follow-up. The tests measure hand dexterity and walking ability, while questionnaires evaluate daily hand use, activities of daily living, fatigue, and mood.
primary_outcomes: 9 Hole Peg Test
title: Telerehabilitation Hand Training for Patients With Neuromuscular Conditions

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to investigate emotional recognition and emotional reactivity in individuals with severe Alcohol Use Disorder (sAUD), Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), comorbid sAUD and depressive symptoms (sAUD+DS), and healthy controls.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Do individuals with sAUD, MDD, sAUD+DS, and healthy controls exhibit different patterns of emotional recognition and emotional reactivity in response to dynamic emotional stimuli?
* How are emotional recognition and emotional reactivity related to each other?
* How are these emotional processes associated with psycho-affective, socio-emotional, stress-related, interoceptive, and disorder-specific factors?
* Do emotional recognition and emotional reactivity predict clinical outcomes at 6- and 12-month follow-up assessments?

Participants will:

* Complete two experimental sessions involving dynamic emotional facial expression and emotional scene tasks
* Provide emotion identification, subjective emotional ratings (type, intensity, and valence), and and self-reported bodily sensations using an emotional body map (InteroMap)
* Undergo eye-tracking, pupillometry, electrodermal activity, and cardiac activity recordings during emotional tasks
* Complete questionnaires assessing psycho-affective, socio-emotional, stress-related, and disorder-specific factors
* Provide saliva and hair samples for cortisol assessment
* Participate in follow-up clinical assessments at 6 and 12 months

Researchers will compare emotional recognition and emotional reactivity profiles across the sAUD, MDD, sAUD+DS, and healthy control groups, and evaluate their predictive value for future clinical outcomes.

brief_summary:
This observational, cross-sectional study examines the relationships between body measurements and athletic performance in elite under-18 male soccer players. The study includes 125 male players aged 17-18 years from professional football club academies competing in the Turkish Football Federation Development League.

The main objective is to investigate whether height, body mass, and body mass index are associated with sprint speed, vertical jump performance, change-of-direction ability, and intermittent endurance. The study also examines the relationships between lower-limb muscle strength and selected athletic performance measures.

Participants undergo a single assessment session consisting of body measurements, countermovement jumps, 10-, 20-, and 30-meter sprint tests, the 505 change-of-direction test, isometric knee-flexor strength measurements, and the Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1.

No training intervention or experimental treatment is administered. The study aims to improve understanding of the physical characteristics associated with athletic performance in elite youth soccer players.
