brief_summary:
The nursing profession is a healthcare discipline that combines theoretical knowledge with clinical practice skills. The primary aim of nursing education is to train healthcare professionals who are prepared for the profession, aware of their duties and responsibilities, and capable of providing effective care to individuals and the community. During their education, nursing students face various challenges both in the academic sphere and in clinical settings. Students are confronted with numerous stressors, such as a heavy course load, preparing for examinations, undertaking clinical placements, a lack of self-confidence, and the changes brought about by the university environment. When this process is not managed effectively, it is thought that students' quality of life and psychological well-being may be adversely affected. Accordingly, there is a need for complementary health approaches to enhance nursing students' quality of life and to safeguard and promote their psychological well-being. Included among these complementary health approaches, laughter therapy has physiological and psychological effects on individuals. There are numerous positive effects associated with laughter, such as improving cognitive functions, enhancing respiration, increasing pain tolerance, improving sleep quality, reducing exam anxiety and lowering stress hormone levels.

Accordingly, the aim of this thesis is to investigate the effect of laughter therapy administered to nursing students on their quality of life and psychological well-being. A review of the literature revealed no existing studies on this topic. Consequently, it is anticipated that this planned thesis will make a significant contribution to filling this gap in the literature.

The study is planned as a randomised controlled experimental study using a pre-test-post-test-follow-up design. The research will be conducted with second-year nursing students at the Faculty of Health Sciences, Çankırı Karatekin University. A total of 112 students who meet the inclusion criteria and are allocated to the experimental (n=56) and control (n=56) groups via randomisation will form the study sample. Experimental group students will undergo a laughter therapy programme comprising a total of eight sessions, at a rate of two sessions per week; the control group will receive no intervention during the study period. Session times will be planned together with the students in the experimental group who will receive laughter therapy. Research data will be collected using the Demographic Information Form, the SF-12 Quality of Life Scale and the Psychological Well-being Scale. IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 24.0, will be used to analyse the data obtained from this study.
primary_outcomes: Change in quality of life measured by the 12-item Quality of Life Scale
title: The Effect of Laughter Therapy on the Quality of Life and Psychological Well-being of Nursing Students

brief_summary:
The goal of this interventional (non-drug, non-device) clinical study is to learn whether children and adolescents born with a cleft lip and/or palate have more tooth decay (dental caries) and more defects of the tooth enamel than children without a cleft, and whether these problems are linked to the type of cleft and to the surgeries these patients have received. In other words, the study aims to find out whether children whose cleft involves the lip and/or the alveolus (the tooth-bearing part of the upper jaw) have a higher risk of caries in the front teeth of the upper jaw.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do children with a cleft have a higher caries experience and a higher caries risk than children of the same age without a cleft? In other words, do children with a cleft involving the lip and/or the alveolus have a higher caries risk in the upper front (maxillary anterior) teeth? Are enamel defects (such as hypomineralisation or hypoplasia) more frequent in children with a cleft, where in the mouth are they mainly located, and are they associated with the cleft type or with specific surgical procedures? Do factors such as parental education level, eating habits, oral hygiene habits and the mobility of the scarred upper lip influence the number and the location of caries lesions? Researchers will compare about 200 patients aged 2 to 18 years with any type of cleft (isolated cleft lip, isolated cleft palate, or cleft lip and alveolus with or without cleft palate; with or without an associated syndrome), followed at the Cleft Lip and Palate Centre of the Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc (Brussels, Belgium), with about 200 children and adolescents of the same age (plus or minus 1 year) without a cleft or syndrome, seen for a routine visit in the paediatric dentistry department of the same hospital.

No drug, device or treatment is tested, and participants' usual care will not be changed. The study adds standardised questionnaires and study-specific clinical assessments to a dental visit that is already planned as part of their regular follow-up. During this visit, participants will:

Have a standard oral examination to record decayed D, missing M and filled F teeth T (DMFT index) in primary and permanent teeth; Have their teeth screened for enamel defects using a standardised European method ( Developmental Defects of Enamel Index ); Have the mobility of their upper lip assessed with a clinical scale (cleft group only), because surgical scars can make brushing of the front teeth more difficult; Possibly have intra-oral photographs taken to document the findings (dental X-rays are only taken if clinically needed for their usual care, never for the study alone).

Parents or legal guardians will fill in short questionnaires about the child's medical and dental history, oral hygiene and eating habits, exposure to protective and risk factors for caries (CAMBRA Caries Management by Risk Assessment), and early-life factors that may be associated with enamel defects.

Participation takes place in a single visit and does not require any additional appointment. There is no direct individual benefit for participants, and the risks are minimal because only routine examinations and questionnaires are used. The results are expected to help identify children with a cleft who are at high risk of caries early on, to show which teeth are most vulnerable, and to design prevention strategies better adapted to these patients (for example, oral hygiene advice and tools adapted to the scarred upper lip).
interventions: Clinical oral examination and standardised questionnaires
lead_sponsor: Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc- Université Catholique de Louvain
primary_outcomes: Caries experience assessed by the dmft/DMFT index in patients with cleft lip and/or palate compared with age-matched controls
title: Risk of Caries and Enamel Abnormalities in Patients With Cleft Palate

brief_summary:
Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease that can progress to cirrhosis and hepatic failure. Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) is the first-line treatment; however, up to 40% of patients exhibit an incomplete biochemical response. Bezafibrate (BZF), a pan-PPAR agonist, has shown promising results when combined with UDCA, improving biochemical parameters and symptoms such as pruritus.

This prospective, randomized, open-label controlled study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of two doses of bezafibrate (400 mg/day vs 800 mg/day) combined with UDCA in patients with PBC over 24 weeks.
primary_outcomes: Normalization of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels
title: Efficacy of Different Doses of Bezafibrate in Combination With Ursodeoxycholic Acid in Patients With Primary Biliary Cholangitis

brief_summary:
Whole-body electromyostimulation is a versatile training technology characterised in particular by its ability to stimulate large muscle groups simultaneously, whilst maintaining an appropriate stimulation intensity for each. Joint-friendly application, time-efficiency, individualised use and, when used correctly , a low risk of injury and damage are among the distinctive features of WB-EMS. Whilst the research focus of WB-EMS lies primarily on preventive and rehabilitative issues , whilst its use in elite sport is not new, the investigation of potential performance enhancement following prior neuromuscular activation ('Post-Activation Performance Enhancement', PAPE) via EMS represents a new research approach. Traditionally, PAPE is predominantly induced by high-intensity strength training, plyometric or ballistic exercises . Electromyostimulation, through its comprehensive neuromuscular activation with comparatively low mechanical load, could be an alternative or complement to these traditional approaches. However, the scientific evidence on EMS-induced PAPE remains The aim of this study is to evaluate the effects of different neuromuscular activation protocols, with and without whole-body EMS, on performance in speed climbing.

The research question is therefore: Can competition performance in speed climbing be enhanced through pre-activation using whole-body EMS? By comparing four different methodological approaches, with and without whole-body EMS, for pre-activation prior to a competition-specific task, the most effective variant of 'Post-Activation Performance Enhancement' (PAPE) will be identified.
primary_outcomes: Speed-climbing performance (seconds)
title: Whole-Body Electromyostimulation and Speed Climbing

brief_summary:
The use of neuromuscular blocking (NMB) agents in modern anesthesia is essential for optimizing surgical exposure and ensuring patient safety. Inadequate neuromuscular recovery at the end of surgery, known as residual curarization, poses significant risks for critical postoperative respiratory complications, aspiration pneumonia, and prolonged recovery times. Therefore, objective neuromuscular monitoring is strongly recommended by international guidelines, including the American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) and the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (ESAIC).

In gynecologic oncology surgery, laparoscopic and robotic approaches often require deep neuromuscular blockade (Post-Tetany Count 1-2) to improve abdominal exposure and allow surgeons to work at lower intraperitoneal pressures. However, the extreme Trendelenburg position and the "tucked-in" positioning of the arms under surgical drapes limit the feasibility of traditional acceleromyography (AMG) monitoring methods. Since AMG devices require free movement of the thumb (m. adductor pollicis), they can yield false-positive or unreliable results when the arms are inaccessible, forcing clinicians to rely on subjective monitoring.

The NMTCuff technology, used by the Vision Duo monitor, measures the neuromuscular response via the contraction pressure of the upper arm muscles (m. triceps/biceps brachii) rather than the wrist. Literature indicates that the response of upper arm muscles correlates better with the diaphragm and laryngeal muscles regarding NMB sensitivity compared to the wrist. This feature suggests that the Vision Duo might detect the recovery of respiratory functions earlier and more reliably.

This study aims to evaluate the correlation and time differences in Train-of-Four (TOF) ratios between the NMTCuff and standard AMG methods during gynecologic oncology surgery. Additionally, it will assess the ease of setup and signal continuity of both devices when the patient's arms remain covered under surgical drapes.

This study is purely prospective and observational in terms of clinical management. The neuromuscular monitoring methods used will not interfere with routine anesthesia care, drug dosing, muscle relaxant reversal strategies, or extubation decisions. The clinician performing the anesthesia management will follow the institutional routine protocol, and data from both devices will only be recorded simultaneously and matched for statistical comparison.
lead_sponsor: Dr Abdurrahman Yurtaslan Ankara Oncology Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Time to Neuromuscular Recovery (TOF Ratio >= 0.90)
title: Comparison of NMTCuff and Standard TOF in Gynecologic Oncology Surgery (NMTCUFF-TOF)

brief_summary:
Congenital ptosis is drooping of the upper eyelid present from birth that can affect vision and appearance. When the eyelid muscle function is good, the eyelid can be corrected by plication (folding and tightening) of the levator muscle that lifts the eyelid.

The main problem with plication is that the eyelid may droop again over time because the smooth muscle surface does not form a strong adhesion. Scraping the muscle surface to create a raw surface may cause scar tissue and stronger adhesion, leading to more stable results.

This randomized study included 50 patients (27 males, 23 females, aged 6 to 32 years) with unilateral congenital ptosis and good levator function greater than 10 mm. Patients were randomly assigned by computer to two groups of 25 patients each. Group A received anterior approach levator plication with scraping of the levator muscle surface using a No. 15 blade until loss of luster and bleeding. Group B received the same plication without scraping. In both groups, three horizontal mattress sutures using 5-0 Ethibond non-absorbable polyester were used.

Eyelid height (Marginal Reflex Distance 1) and patient satisfaction were measured at 1 week, 4 weeks, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks after surgery. The study aims to determine if scraping leads to more consistent and permanent eyelid height.

This is a retrospective registration of a completed study conducted at Zagazig University Hospitals, Egypt, approved by the Institutional Review Board.
interventions: Levator resection with levator muscle scraping
primary_outcomes: Change in Marginal Reflex Distance 1 (MRD1)
title: Anterior Approach Levator Plication for Congenital Ptosis, With or Without Scraping of the Levator Muscle Surface

brief_summary: Population aging in Brazil is accompanied by an increased prevalence of cardiovascular diseases and a decline in cardiac autonomic modulation. Given this scenario, physical training emerges as an essential non-pharmacological intervention to mitigate the impacts of senescence. This study aims to investigate the effects of concurrent training (CT) on cardiac autonomic modulation and behavioral aspects in older adults, comparing it to resistance training (RT) and endurance training (ET) performed in isolation. The methodology consists of a prospective clinical trial involving a projected sample of 78 participants aged 60 years or older. The interventions last 12 weeks, with a frequency of three sessions per week. Assessments include heart rate variability (HRV)-analyzed in both time and frequency domains-hemodynamic parameters (blood pressure and double product), biochemical markers of lipid and glycemic profiles, and instruments to measure sleep quality and perceived stress.

brief_summary: Le Fort I osteotomy is a common jaw surgery that includes a step called pterygomaxillary dysjunction, during which force applied with a surgical instrument (osteotome) can be transmitted toward the eye socket (orbit) and the optic nerve canal. Serious eye complications after this surgery are rare, but it is not known whether smaller, subclinical changes occur in the optic nerve that go unnoticed without special testing. This study uses a non-invasive eye imaging test called optical coherence tomography (OCT) to measure the thickness of the nerve fiber layer around the optic nerve, before and after Le Fort I surgery, to find out whether such changes occur.

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled clinical trial aims to evaluate the effects of different opioid analgesics on gastrointestinal recovery after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery.

Opioid medications are commonly used to manage pain after surgery, but they may cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, and delayed recovery of bowel function. Biased μ-opioid receptor agonists, such as tegileridine and oliceridine, may provide effective pain relief with fewer gastrointestinal side effects than conventional opioids.

The main question is whether biased opioid receptor agonists can shorten the time to postoperative gastrointestinal recovery compared with sufentanil, a conventional opioid analgesic.

The study plans to enroll 212 adults undergoing elective gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups:

* Lower-dose tegileridine
* Higher-dose tegileridine
* Oliceridine
* Sufentanil

After surgery, participants will receive the assigned medication through a patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) pump.

The primary outcome is time to gastrointestinal recovery (GI-2), defined as the time from the end of surgery until both the first bowel movement (defecation) and tolerance of solid food have occurred. The later of these two events determines the GI-2 recovery time.

Researchers will also assess the time to first passage of flatus, postoperative nausea and vomiting, gastrointestinal function scores, pain intensity, gastrointestinal ultrasound findings, analgesic requirements, and medication-related adverse events.

The findings may help determine whether biased opioid receptor agonists offer advantages over conventional opioid analgesics in supporting gastrointestinal recovery while maintaining adequate postoperative pain control.
primary_outcomes: Time to Gastrointestinal Recovery (GI-2)
title: Effects of Biased Opioid Agonists on Gastrointestinal Recovery After Gynecologic Laparoscopic Surgery

brief_summary: Dental trauma in children may require prompt decisions by parents or caregivers. This three-arm randomized trial will compare a mobile application, an artificial intelligence chatbot, and a printed dental-trauma first-aid booklet as methods of delivering parental education. Approximately 220 parents or legal guardians will be allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio and will receive their assigned educational resource over four weeks. Parental dental-trauma knowledge and accuracy of responses to simulated emergency scenarios will be assessed at four weeks, with follow-up assessments at 12 weeks. Additional measures include confidence, usability, engagement, recognition of avulsion management, and anxiety. The study is planned in Selangor, Malaysia.

Dental Trauma Emergency Decision-Making Accuracy at Week 4

brief_summary: Resistance training (RT) is a widely used strategy to improve strength in older adults and counteract age-related decline. Combining RT with creatine monohydrate (CrM) supplementation has been shown to enhance exercise-induced improvements in muscle status and physical performance in this population. Cluster-set resistance training (CS-RT) is a relatively recent approach that has not yet been explored in combination with CrM supplementation in this population. Thus, this study aims to investigate the effects of an 8-week CS-RT program with and without CrM supplementation on body composition and physical performance in older adults. Thirty-six older adults over 60 years of age, with no prior RT experience, will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: CS-RT+CrM (n=12, 0.1 g·kg-¹·day-¹ of CrM), CS-RT without CrM supplementation (n=12), and a control group (CG) maintaining usual daily activities. The 8-week CS-RT program will include three sessions per week with 48 hours of rest between sessions. Each session will consist of three sets of 3 blocks × 4 repetitions at 75% of 1RM, with 30-second intra-set rest and 2-minute rest intervals between sets and exercises (lower limbs: half squat, leg extension, leg press, calf raise; upper limbs: chest press, lat pulldown, shoulder press, biceps/triceps curls). Concentric repetitions will be performed at maximal intended velocity. Body composition will be assessed using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), physical performance with the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), and maximal strength using a one-repetition maximum (1RM) test following ACSM and NSCA guidelines. Statistical analysis will include an ANCOVA with pre-test scores as a covariate, followed by post hoc tests and effect size calculations. Additionally, a difference-in-differences estimation approach will be employed to assess changes over time, with statistical significance set at p \< 0.05. The investigators hypothesize that CS-RT+CrM will result in greater improvements on body composition (reduction of fat mass and increase of fat-free mass), physical performance, and maximal strength compared to CS-RT alone. This clinical trial was approved by the Academic Unit of the Postgraduate and Research Department of the Autonomous University of Baja California - Tijuana Campus, Mexico (Code: 340/4188).

brief_summary: Chest radiography is widely used in emergency departments, resuscitation rooms, intensive care units, and other acute-care settings. Clinically important abnormalities may be missed because findings are subtle, uncommon, obscured by overlapping anatomy, or encountered under high workload. This pragmatic randomized trial evaluates whether EvoXRare, an artificial intelligence system that provides a draft chest radiograph report and high-risk alerts for uncommon or clinically important abnormalities, reduces clinically important diagnostic misses compared with routine physician interpretation alone. Approximately 70,000 adults will be randomized 1:1 across 15-20 hospitals in China. The primary endpoint is the patient-level rate of clinically important abnormalities present on the reference standard but not reported in the initial clinical interpretation. Key secondary outcomes include detection of rare or easily missed findings, time to recognition of critical abnormalities, report turnaround time, false-positive alerts, additional imaging, recall/communication events, and selected short-term clinical outcomes.
interventions: Experimental: EvoXRare AI-Assisted Chest Radiograph Interpretation.
lead_sponsor: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Patient-Level Clinically Important Abnormality Miss Rate on the Index Chest Radiograph
title: EvoXRare AI-Assisted Interpretation of Emergency Chest Radiographs
